title: Voyager 1 Is Almost One Light-Day Away
summary:
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is close to an amazing milestone. Soon, it will be one light-day from Earth. That means even light — the fastest thing there is — needs a whole day to travel from the spacecraft to us.

Voyager 1 left Earth in 1977, almost 50 years ago. It is the farthest spacecraft ever built, and it has flown into the space between the stars.

The spacecraft is running low on power. It loses about 4 watts of power every year. So in September, engineers finished a careful project. They replaced three devices with new ones that use less electricity. This should keep Voyager 1's science tools working longer.

In October, the spacecraft's signal suddenly stopped for about two days, then came back on its own. One set of small engines had stopped working, and the spacecraft had switched to backup engines by itself. "We have to expect the unexpected," said mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.
why_it_matters: Voyager 1 is like a message from Earth traveling between the stars, and it shows how far human-made things can go.
